newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's ex-leaders Chun, Roh storm out of court.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's ex-leaders Chun, Roh storm out of court.

text.p: Former South Korean presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo on Thursday stormed out a courtroom in protest against the forced appearance at their appeals trial of their predecessor Choi Kyu-hah, state television reported.
They made their dramatic walkout shortly before Choi entered the courtroom, it said. Choi refused to take an oath when he appeared, the television station added.

Roh's defence lawyer told the judge the appearance in the same court of three former heads of state was not in the public interest, the Korea Broadcasting System said. When the judge rejected the argument, Roh and Chun stormed out.

Choi, 77, was caretaker head of state for 10 turbulent months between the assassination of presidential strongman Park Chung-hee in October 1979 and Chun's violent grab for power following a coup in December of that year.

Chun was sentenced to death after being convicted of masterminding the coup, ordering a massacre of pro-democracy demonstrators in May 1980 in the southern city of Kwangju and amassing a slush fund worth hundreds of millions of dollars from corporate pay-offs.
Roh was sentenced to 22-1/2 years in jail on similar charges of mutiny, treason and bribery. Both are appealing the verdicts.
